references.text: Introduces Noah's sons as the ancestors of all peoples on earth after the flood
First mention by name of Noah's three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth
Repeats the names of Noah's three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth
Uses the same 'toledot' formula ('this is the history of') as a structural key phrase in Genesis
The genealogy leading from Shem to Abram, linking Noah's descendants to the patriarchs of Israel
Parallel genealogy of Noah's sons and their descendants in 1 Chronicles
Refers to Noah's family who survived the flood, with eight souls saved through water
Genesis 9:18 confirms that the same three sons left the ark, which is the direct basis for the genealogical account in 10:1.
1 Chronicles 1:4 confirms and repeats the genealogy from Genesis 10:1 as part of a broader historical overview.
Genesis 10:32 serves as the theological conclusion to the introductory heading in 10:1.
Genesis 11:10 complements the general overview in 10:1 by beginning the specific genealogy of Shem.
Genesis 7:13 shows the same three sons entering the ark, which is the basis for their role as ancestors in 10:1.
Genesis 10:21 gives theological depth to Shem's place in the list from 10:1 by connecting him to Eber and the line of Abraham.
Luke 3:36 shows how the genealogy from 10:1 culminates in Jesus, who is the ancestor of all believers.
